My experience with East Cowes Medical Practice has been extremely distressing and unsafe. I contacted the surgery after my mental health significantly declined after coming off of tablets and was told by the mental health team to get in touch to restart my medication. Despite clearly explaining that I was struggling and deteriorating daily, the receptionist refused to book me a GP appointment and insisted on sending me through triage, this triage was actually never logged and I had to chase and ended up going through triage again!

After over a week of waiting for a call from the mental health team as advised and promised, I found out I hadn’t even been referred to the correct team, I had been put through to get another triage team, who couldn’t help or give me the medication I needed. When I begged for an emergency GP appointment again, I was told that “mental health doesn’t count as an emergency” and advised to go to A&E, despite me explaining that I suffer from health anxiety and physically could not cope with that environment or even get there. I was then told to ring 111. This advice was completely inappropriate and showed a worrying lack of training or understanding of mental health.

I rang 111, who called the doctors and requested I be seen as an emergency. I got a call back from the receptionist once again denying me this and claiming 111 had no power to do this - despite them telling me to go to 111. I called once more the next day and 111 once again sent a message and requested I be seen ASAP - I have still not heard back.

I was repeatedly denied medication that I’ve been safely prescribed for years, and TWO NHS 111 request for a same-day GP callback was ignored. To make matters worse, one of my previous triage requests disappeared from their system entirely, which raises serious concerns about their record-keeping.

The whole experience left me feeling dismissed, hopeless, and at risk. Mental health should be treated with the same urgency and respect as physical health, but East Cowes Medical has failed to meet even the most basic standards of care, compassion, and patient safety. Triage does not work and reception staff seriously need urgent training in mental health and how to talk to
